heading: Deep networks fit random labels without changing architecture or training hyperparameters
definition: standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods reach zero or near-zero training error on a completely random labeling of the training set (test error at chance), without changing the architecture or training hyperparameters.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce random-label fitting, with WideResNet-18 showing test performance near chance after fitting random labels. Keeping training hyperparameters unchanged is disputed: VGG-19 required a lower learning rate.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: fitting-component support, ? for complete V1; 1-10B: R0 for fitting component, ? for complete V1; 10-100B: R0 for fitting component (one study, sharing no authors with an original: image-adapted Qwen3-14B fits nearly completely on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 but incompletely on TinyImageNet-200), ? for complete V1; >100B: ? with no coverage. Toy settings are not separately bucketed. Size-unstated image experiments support R2 for conditional fitting with chance testing, while unrestricted V1 is contested.
suggested_status.reason: C applies to V1 as written, especially its unchanged-hyperparameters clause. WideResNet-18 independently reproduces perfect fitting and approximately chance testing under a common SGD protocol (arXiv:1904.12286#R1, arXiv:1904.12286#R12), supporting the conditional capability. However, VGG-19 fails at its clean-label learning rate and requires a reduction (arXiv:1906.04659#R7 and its text-only challenges verdict). At larger scales, Llama 3 8B supplies near-zero training loss with LoRA, without chance-test or numerical classification-error endpoints (arXiv:2406.17642#R1); language-pretrained, image-adapted Qwen3-14B under random bridge-label training reaches 97.9% and 97.7% training accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, observed nearly complete fitting (arXiv:2604.01833#R32, arXiv:2604.01833#R33), but only 94.3% on TinyImageNet-200, which remains incomplete (arXiv:2604.01833#R34). These Qwen rows report training accuracy only, and V1 sets no numerical near-zero threshold. counts.json versions.V1.studies_by_size and versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size establish the covered size buckets, but do not establish every V1 clause within them.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched clean-label/random-label experiments with fixed architecture, optimizer, regularization and stopping rules, reporting training classification error and chance-calibrated test performance, would determine whether the unchanged-recipe clause survives within a specified scope. Define near-zero numerically before comparing endpoints. At 1-10B and 10-100B, establish the complete conjunction beyond adapted-model training fit; >100B remains untested in the supplied coverage.

source.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

original_result.setup: Zhang et al. trained networks on randomly labeled CIFAR10 and ImageNet under different regularization settings.
original_result.result: With weight decay on CIFAR10, Inception and MLP 3x512 reached 100% training accuracy, while Alexnet failed to converge. On ImageNet, Inception V3 reached 87.81–95.20% top-1 training accuracy across the reported regularization settings.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

wording_issues.issue: Capacity and trainable-layer restrictions are unspecified. Narrow MLPs and frozen-layer CNN/DenseNet configurations fit incompletely. MemRandomLast uses randomly initialized DenseNet121 parameters with the backbone frozen and only the last two layers trainable. The original small classical MLP and CNN remain near chance on random-label MNIST; enlarging the MLP improves training accuracy without establishing complete fitting. Parameter-budget sweeps likewise distinguish incomplete from complete fitting.

wording_issues.phrase: standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods
wording_issues.issue: Supporting evidence includes shallow attention-only models, specialized normalization networks, and conditional full-batch GD or gradient-flow guarantees. These require their own assumptions. Width-256 LN-G networks with 128 groups and depths 6–14 remain near guessing on both random-label datasets; this limits extension to the specialized two-neuron-group architecture rather than challenging V1 within its stated standard-network scope. The tested depth-4 ViT baseline has a best three-seed mean training accuracy of 48.2%.

wording_issues.phrase: reach zero or near-zero training error
wording_issues.issue: The statement needs capacity and training-procedure conditions. ResNet-18 reaches 89.5% training accuracy after 100 SGD epochs without augmentation; augmented ResNet-110 reaches training accuracy fraction 0.24 after 200 Adam epochs. A maximum-load depth-3, width-32 toy network shows qualitative learning failure after 2000 epochs, with exact training accuracy not stated, and VGG11 fails under its tested 200-epoch multi-step schedule.

Near-zero has no numerical definition, and verdict thresholds differ. AllConv at 97.80% training accuracy is accepted, while an MLP at 98.06% is treated as incomplete. GPT-2's 1.3% error is accepted. Language-pretrained Qwen3-14B training accuracies of 97.9% and 97.7% should likewise be treated as observed nearly complete fitting, rather than independently establishing scope limits. ImageNet top-5 accuracy also does not establish top-1 interpolation.

wording_issues.phrase: without changing the architecture or training hyperparameters
wording_issues.issue: VGG-19 requires lowering its initial learning rate from 0.1 to 0.01. Conventional VGG experiments use 800 random-label epochs versus 100–400 true-label epochs, changing the budget and epoch-based learning-rate schedule. ImageNet-initialized ResNet-152 and ResNet-18 FaceScrub fitting lowers the rate from 0.001 to 0.0001; permuted-label training accuracy fractions are respectively 0.996 and 0.994, compared with non-permuted baselines of 1.000. PreResNet-20 fits perfectly after disabling weight decay and augmentation and lowering its initial rate to 0.01. The VGG and PreResNet results qualify the unchanged-hyperparameters clause; PreResNet failure under unchanged settings and chance test performance are not established.

Successful settings include st-VGG with both dropout layers removed, enlargement of the ordinary MLP to MLP++, modified ResNet18/VGG11 encoders with MLP projectors, and pretrained Llama with a frozen backbone and trainable LoRA adapters. These findings require their architecture and adaptation conditions.

wording_issues.phrase: on a completely random labeling of the training set
wording_issues.issue: Some evidence concerns partial corruption, random subsets mixed with clean data, or labels shared across correlated examples. ResNet-34 uses 40% label randomization; RATT mixes clean and randomly labeled examples; MRI labels are randomized by subject and shared across slices. Code localization uses task-specific structured corruption, with complete corruption causing prediction collapse.

Randomization mechanisms require source definitions. CIFAR-10 symmetric noise ε=0.9 produces uniform label-independent assignments. SNR=0.01 instead gives nearly random continuous regression targets. The sequence-depth study permutes distinct labels rather than sampling from a fixed class set. MNIST UI corruption excludes the clean class and differs from independent uniform relabeling.

Training fit and chance testing must be established together under the stated test distribution. The fine-grained two-layer study randomizes test labels. Llama/Mistral fitting lacks held-out random-target error. The MNIST cohort supplies chance testing without achieved training errors, while subject-split MRI supplies approximately chance testing with incomplete training fitting.

Reported measures are not interchangeable. Near-zero training loss and cross-entropy below 0.05 are not directly reported classification-error rates. For the MNIST MLP at rho=1 and epoch 200, SU gives M=0.86 and PERM gives M=0.88. M is the fraction of changed-label samples predicted with their noisy label, not overall training accuracy. Near-zero language-model training loss does not supply a numerical exact-answer error rate.

method_sensitivity.what: On 60,000 randomly labeled MNIST examples, ReLU-MLPs achieve 11.7%, 18.2%, 47.6% and 100.0% training accuracy at parameter budgets P≤5k, 20k, 100k and 500k after 200 epochs with condition-specific optimizer/rate selection. Acoustic-scene ResNet fitting rises from 85.51% at W=32 to 100% at W=64, with D=1 and K=1. A fixed-dimension attention-only model perfectly memorizes approximately 550 examples with H=4 and 1300 with H=8. SNLI Encoder fitting rises from around 87% with 611 subwords to more than 98% with 18,336; LM and MLM reach 100% with larger vocabularies.

CNN/DenseNet clean-label retraining with all layers trainable reaches 99.85–100% randomized-label training accuracy; selected frozen-layer CNN settings reach only 17.31–91.38%. Full T5-base fine-tuning eventually perfectly memorizes random word associations, whereas prompt-tuning a frozen backbone with 100 trainable embeddings remains incomplete and takes over 200k updates to begin nontrivial learning. Image-adapted GPT-2 achieves 93.9% versus 34.2% training accuracy on random-label CIFAR-10 with language-pretrained versus scratch initialization; CIFAR-100 values are 98.7% versus 65.9%. A ReLU head with frozen ViT features and an eight-dimensional bottleneck reaches only 39.1% agreement after 60 epochs on randomized PathMNIST.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning rate, batch size, schedule and optimization budget
method_sensitivity.what: VGG-19 fails to learn random labels at its clean-label initial learning rate 0.1 and requires 0.01. A separate VGG-11 experiment explicitly fails to fit all-random CIFAR-10 labels under its tested 200-epoch multi-step schedule. The geometry study reports poor high-corruption training with typical hyperparameters and adopts a smaller learning rate and larger batch size. Successful small-Transformer runs reach 99% random-label training accuracy, while learning rate 0.01 fails to reach saturation within 5,000 epochs on both random and modular data. These are reported procedure qualifications; they do not establish that schedule alone explains cross-study differences.

Under a common randomized-CIFAR100 WideResNet-28-10 recipe, training errors are vanilla 1.22% (observed near-zero fitting), Spectral 17.24% and Stable-30/SRN-30 29.04% (partial). Width-256 LN-G networks with 16 or 32 groups nearly perfectly fit CIFAR-10-RL; specialized 128-group configurations remain near guessing at 10.22–10.38% across reported datasets. A depth-4, width-128 normalization-only CNN reaches 24.6% with full-map LN, 95.8% with best conventional GN and 100.0% with position-wise PLN after 200 SGD epochs. Matched toy architecture variants use the Any criterion: MLP inclusion and normalization increase fitted facts, excluding anomalous MLP-present, norms-on, residual-off, bias-off ReLU configurations from positive comparisons. Mixing compares dual embedding against uniform attention and uniform against learned attention; main-text and appendix ranges disagree. Mixing options perform equally without both MLP and norms. Learned attention is least stable across repeated runs.

method_sensitivity.factor: Explicit regularization, information constraints and activation noise
method_sensitivity.what: Small AlexNet, All-CNN and ResNet completely fit random labels at sufficiently low β below the observed transition before β=1; stronger information-bottleneck penalties cause empirical underfitting. Residual memorization is unreported, leaving partial versus absent unresolved; complete prevention at β>1 is theoretical. Added penalties and stochastic weights change standard training, so these results describe method sensitivity. Small-inception shuffled-label training accuracy progressively declines with Gaussian activation noise, reaching chance only at sufficiently strong noise after 100 epochs; ReLU networks require about 5 times more noise than Sigmoid networks for a similar decline. Stochastic CEB and VIB models with ρ<6 do not learn fixed random Fashion MNIST labels within 100 epochs. As original-source baseline material, Alexnet with weight decay fails to converge on random-label CIFAR10.

FastResNet with standard average gradients and Adam memorizes fully randomized CIFAR-10; the study reports that increasing its AND-mask agreement threshold quickly hinders memorization, without a separate numerical masked-training endpoint. ResNet-18 with CE or CE-fix fits full corruption, while supervised contrastive loss on CIFAR10 misses exact zero error within 100k iterations. Its unreported residual error leaves V1's zero-or-near-zero fitting unresolved; the exact-zero failure bears on V2 and V4. Self-adaptive training and self-adaptive mixup (alpha=0.2) yield 10.2% training and 10% test accuracy on entirely random CIFAR-10 labels. Synthetic Random-dataset MLP training-accuracy fractions are 1.00 ± 0.00 with CE and 0.98 ± 0.04 with MSE.

TRADES nearly perfectly fits random-label CIFAR-10, including reported DenseNet-121 and DLA extensions. PGD adversarial training fails to converge at tested budgets ε≥2/255, including larger WRN-34-20 and WRN-70-16 configurations and tested adversary or training changes. Reducing the PGD-AT budget to 1/255 permits convergence. These thresholds belong to the tested configurations; natural-input accuracy and robust accuracy remain separate measures.

Encoder-projector networks fit fixed random labels with standard augmentation, but independently randomizing augmented samples makes fitting infeasible within 5000 epochs as augmentation multiplicity grows. The ResNet-110 study reports training accuracy fraction 0.24 on completely randomized CIFAR-10 under its augmented recipe and attributes difficult high-noise fitting to augmentation. The membership study reports reduced memorization capacity with augmentation; its numerical comparison uses different positive-image counts, preventing a fixed-sample attribution.

A custom quadratic MNIST network fits random numerical labels poorly on original inputs, while Gaussian perturbations with standard deviation 0.01 per coordinate enable very accurate fitting. In the MNIST corruption study, complete SU and PERM corruption yield memorized fractions M=0.86 and 0.88, with 10.1% clean-test accuracy; UI yields M=0.962. M measures fitting among changed-label samples, rather than overall training accuracy, and UI excludes the clean class. Under complete task-specific structured corruption, Transformer, GGNN and GREAT VarMisuse localization models collapse toward predicting every sample bug-free. These constructions do not establish interchangeable random-label interventions.

With subject-level OASIS-random splits, VGG16-v1, VGG16-v2 and ResNet-18 achieve training accuracies 63.38%, 69.17% and 84.49%, with approximately chance testing. Slice-level splits yield training accuracies 100%, 100% and 99.09% and inflated held-out performance. Labels are randomized by subject and shared across slices, so changing the split changes which correlated examples enter training and testing. The matching MRI records require version/duplicate reconciliation before independent-evidence counting.

status_amendment.public_note: For models of 10 to 100 billion parameters, the 14B Qwen model's 97.9% and 97.7% training accuracy on randomly labelled CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 now counts as nearly complete fitting; only its 94.3% on TinyImageNet-200 is still counted as incomplete. The overall level is unchanged.
